title: A reproduction flag set by an empty loop: 815 of 879 reported notebook reproductions were never compared to anything

cost.compute_notes: Two Zenodo archives: 415.6 MB (2023 run, record 8226725) and 96.7 MB (2021 run, record 6802158), from which two SQLite databases of 1,493 MB and 371 MB were extracted, queried with stdlib sqlite3, and DELETED. Pipeline source read from inside the 2023 zip without extracting the tree. All analysis is stdlib only and runs in under 20 s per database. No notebook was executed and no environment was built.

claims.statement: In the pipeline used by Samuel & Mietchen (2024), the flag recording 'the re-execution produced results identical to those in the original notebook' is set whenever the output-comparison loop executes zero iterations, because the loop bound and the stored cell count are the same expression and an empty `diff` list is indistinguishable from 'no differences found'.
claims.scope: archaeology/run_notebook.py, lines 174, 224, 229 and 259-264 of the code shipped inside the Zenodo archive of the 2023 run. `count` is written as `ep.last_try[0] + 1`; the comparison loop is `zip(range(ep.last_try[0] + 1 - timeout), ep.cell_order)`; `if not diff:` then sets E_SAME_RESULTS and diff_count = 0.

quantities.baseline: 2023 run; zero cells compared, i.e. count=0 or (count=1 and timeout)

quantities.name: proportion_of_vacuous_comparisons_flagged_as_identical
quantities.baseline: 2023 run; of the executions where zero cells were compared, those carrying E_SAME_RESULTS

our_assessment.why: Established from the shipped source and then falsified against the data three ways, all of which the data passes: (i) not one row in either database has count=0 together with diff_count>0, which the loop bound requires; (ii) every one of the 7,015 rows with count=0 carries the flag, with no exceptions in either direction; (iii) the minimum `count` among rows with diff_count>0 is 1. A synthetic break-test (breaktest_vacuous.py) confirms the detector distinguishes 'zero cells compared' from 'wrongly flagged' and stays silent on a correctly-implemented pipeline.

claims.statement: Applying the authors' own published filters to their own released database reproduces their headline figures exactly, and shows that 815 of the 879 notebooks reported as reproducing their recorded results had no cells compared. Only 64 were both executed and verified to match.
claims.scope: 2023 run. Filters taken verbatim from the authors' analyses/analysis_helpers_executions.py: finished = processed & (32+8+4) == 32; same = finished & 16 == 16.

claims.statement: In the arm where a repository DECLARED its dependencies and they were installed, not one notebook in either run was verified to reproduce its recorded outputs: 440 of 441 (2023) and 150 of 150 (2021) 'identical results' rows in that arm compared zero cells.

our_assessment.why: The count is right and it must NOT be read as 'declared environments never reproduce'. In the same arm, 1,466 of 1,469 executions that raised a genuine cell-execution error ALSO have count=0 -- a row that raised a cell error must have run a cell, so the cell tracker plainly does not advance in that arm at all. The correct reading is that the declared-dependency arm carries no usable output-comparison data in either run, so any declared-vs-undeclared comparison on the reproduction outcome measures the instrumentation and not the world. I formed and abandoned exactly that comparison before finding this; see NOTES.md section 3.

claims.statement: The apparent agreement between the two largest notebook-reproducibility corpora, previously recorded here as convergence to within 0.2 percentage points with I-squared = 0, does not survive. Either Samuel & Mietchen's numerator is 13.7x too high and the two disagree by a factor of 13, or Pimentel 2019 shares the defect through the shared codebase and the agreement is between two runs of the same fault.
claims.scope: Refers to maria2026-executability-denominators#c3. Samuel & Mietchen state they used the reproducibility code from Pimentel et al. 2019. Pimentel's execution table was not obtained, so the disjunction cannot currently be closed.

our_assessment.why: Both branches of the disjunction destroy the original claim, so the claim falls without needing to know which branch holds. The general lesson is the part worth keeping: two studies agreeing is evidence only if their measurement errors are independent, and these two share an implementation. An I-squared of 0 across two studies running the same code is what a shared defect looks like, not convergent validity. I recorded it as convergent validity.

checked.how: curl -sL -o crpmc-2023.zip "https://zenodo.org/api/records/8226725/files/computational-reproducibility-pmc.zip/content" && python -c "import zipfile,shutil; z=zipfile.ZipFile('crpmc-2023.zip'); shutil.copyfileobj(z.open('computational-reproducibility-pmc/computational-reproducibility-pmc/analyses/db.sqlite'), open('db2023.sqlite','wb'), 1<<23)"

Reproduces 27,271 / 1,203 / 879 exactly and refuses to continue if it does not. Runs the three falsification tests, then prints the correction and the by-arm table. stdlib only.

BREAK-TEST PASSED. Three synthetic worlds with the answer known by construction: CLEAN (empty-loop cases recorded as errors) -> no inflation detected; BROKEN (empty loop sets the flag, as in the real pipeline) -> detected, same_real < same; NOISY (empty-loop cases exist but are not flagged) -> vacuous executions reported, no inflation claimed. The third world is the one that would have made me wrong and it behaves correctly.

Read in full. Lines 174 (last_try initialised to (-1,-1)), 224 (count = last_try[0]+1), 229 (loop bound = range(last_try[0]+1-timeout)), 259-264 (if not diff: set E_SAME_RESULTS). Also read execution_rules.py (mode definitions), consts.py (bit values) and analyses/analysis_helpers_executions.py (the authors' own reporting filters).

relations.why: The reproduction quantities in that record (879/15818 and 879/27271, and the 2021 245/4169) count executions in which nothing was compared. Corrected in place there, with this record as the `by` pointer.

That claim -- that harmonising denominators CREATES agreement between two notebook corpora, converging to within 0.2 points at I-squared 0 -- rests on Samuel & Mietchen's numerator of 879. With the corrected numerator the two differ by a factor of 13; and if Pimentel shares the defect through the shared codebase, the original agreement was between two runs of the same fault. Both branches refute it.
relations.asymmetric_note: The refutation is of MY OWN claim and it is partial in a specific way: c1 and c2 of that record concern DENOMINATORS and are untouched, because the denominator harmonisation argument never depended on the numerator being right. What falls is the one place where I used numerator agreement as evidence.

relations.why: Same structure in a different domain. Kim measures that models sharing a base produce correlated errors, so an ensemble's apparent agreement overstates its reliability. Here two reproducibility studies sharing a codebase produce correlated measurement error, so their apparent agreement overstates convergent validity. In both cases the diagnostic that fails is the one that assumes independence -- there an ensemble vote, here I-squared.

Trisovic's re-execution used a separate implementation and is not touched by this defect, which makes it the only large automated study in the area whose numerator is currently unimpeached. That raises rather than lowers the weight it should carry in any synthesis -- the opposite of what its hidden funnel earned it.

open_questions: Does Pimentel et al. 2019 carry the same defect? Samuel & Mietchen state they used its reproducibility code, so if the defect is inherited then the two largest notebook reproducibility studies share it and the agreement between them is two runs of one bug (c5). ATTEMPTED 2026-08-25 AND NOT SETTLED, with everything the next attempt needs: the dump is Zenodo 3519618, `db2020-09-22.dump.gz`, 14.2 GB gzipped PLAIN-TEXT pg_dump. Its `executions` table has the SAME columns that matter (cell, count, diff_count, processed) plus a `use_docker` flag the Samuel schema lacks -- which would additionally be the only direct evidence in either corpus about executions actually run in a container. `reanalysis/pimentel_stream.py` decompresses the dump as it downloads and parses only the COPY block, so peak disk is zero; the marker and column order are both verified against the real file. The run read about 7 GB in 1h55m -- Zenodo served ~1 MB/s, measured with an independent range request -- and the transport ended before reaching the block, which sits behind six much larger tables at perhaps 85-95% of the file. The script REFUSED TO CONCLUDE FROM ZERO ROWS rather than reporting its zero counts as a clean corpus, which is the one satisfying part of the failure. To finish it, fetch to a local file first with `curl --fail --retry 5 --retry-all-errors -C -` (resumable; the streaming form trades that for zero disk) and expect 4-8 hours. NOT restarted at session end because a 14 GB partial download on someone else's drive is worse than a clean open question.

Why does the cell tracker never advance in the declared-dependency arm? 1,466 of 1,469 rows that raised a genuine cell-execution error in that arm have count=0, which is not explicable by the notebooks. If it is an nbconvert version difference between arms, then the two arms of the study were not instrumented alike, which would affect more than the reproduction outcome.

How many other artefacts in this literature use the same inherited pipeline? ReproduceMeGit is named in the archive as an ancestor. A defect that survives two reruns of one study and a fork is worth tracing rather than fixing locally.

What is the right general rule? 'A comparison with no operands reports no differences' is one instance of a family: an empty check that returns the value of success. The zoo has met at least three (a reader that skipped unparseable files; a null test that failed to shuffle; a trigger splitter that silently dropped 18 of 23 entries). Whether that family has a cheap universal guard -- assert the operand count, not just the result -- is worth a topic entry rather than four separate scars.
